title: Design depth into flat frames
principle: Interfaces are flat canvases pretending to be rooms. Rauno Freiberg’s Designing Depth argues you convey story and dimensionality the way film does: dirty the frame with layered foreground/background, blur backdrops to drop Z-axis, choreograph motion so layers read as stacked surfaces—not decorative chrome.
procedure: Name the focal subject and the ambient layers that should sit in front of / behind it (props, out-of-focus objects, offset frames).
Lower non-focal surfaces on the Z-axis with blur, dim, or fade-to-infinite edges—especially when an overlay claims focus.
When revealing overlays, decide which backdrop layers stay interactive vs must de-emphasize (blur/dim signals not actionable).
Prefer reusing primary subjects as depth cues (e.g. offset browser frames that also communicate product abundance) over gimmick decorations.
Verify with a screenshot critic: does the composition feel layered, or still like stickers on a flat board?
examplePrompts:
Audit this UI for flatness. Apply Designing Depth (Rauno Freiberg):
1) Identify focal subject vs ambient foreground/background layers.
2) Blur or dim backdrops when overlays open so Z-axis reads correctly.
3) Add one intentional dirty-frame cue (offset surface, soft edge fade, out-of-focus prop) that also communicates product meaning—not ornament.
4) Do not add purple chrome, glassmorphism, or decorative orbs.
Return: before/after notes + the CSS/structure changes.

This modal feels pasted on. Recompose so the backdrop clearly sits behind: dim + slight blur the page, keep only the modal actionable, fade the modal bottom edge if content continues. Cite depth-of-field intent in a one-line comment.
promptWhy: Forces the model to treat depth as composition (focal vs ambient) instead of dumping glass/shadow chrome.
Names the affordance signal (backdrop not actionable) so dim/blur is not decorative.
tips: Film parallel: dirtying the frame with foreground obstruction carries emotion a pristine head-on shot lacks.
Blurred backdrops on overlays mimic natural depth of field and prevent false affordance on the page behind.
Depth cues should reinforce product story (abundance of previews, stacked layers)—not random decoration.
Public essay: https://rauno.me/craft/depth — paraphrase only; no endorsement.

workedExamples.title: Marketing frame that fell flat
workedExamples.before: Browser frame + overlays dropped on a page with no Z separation—surfaces read as a sloppy afterthought.
workedExamples.after: Inner background blurred (lowered on Z), bottom edge faded to feel infinite; offset frames and soft props reuse the primary subjects to show abundance.
workedExamples.body: From Rauno’s Designing Depth (public, July 2024): depth comes from layered composition and meaningful reuse of subjects, not stickers. Cite: rauno.me/craft/depth.

workedExamples.title: Overlay without false affordance
workedExamples.body: iOS-style context menus dim/blur the Home Screen so only the menu feels actionable. Skipping de-emphasis signals the whole backdrop is still interactive—which is wrong. Apply the same rule to web modals and drawers.

workedExamples.title: Quiet Folio restraint
workedExamples.body: On this paper/ink desk, depth is hairline rules, folio numerals, and restrained motion—not frosted glass. Depth is not glassmorphism.

antiPatterns: Adding glassmorphism / glow orbs and calling it depth.
Blur that does not change affordance (backdrop still looks clickable).
Decorative layers that do not communicate product meaning.
checklist: Focal vs ambient layers named in the brief or PR.
Overlays de-emphasize backdrop (dim/blur) when backdrop is not actionable.
At least one depth cue reuses a primary subject, not a random ornament.
Screenshot critic no longer tags the layout as flat stickers.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Stop when the named task is clearer and acceptance evidence is recorded; do not add polish without a problem.
